text:
LAK built a 5-1 lead by the middle of the second period on chances that were mostly modest. Taylor Ward opened the scoring 75 seconds in, and Brandt Clarke tipped in a second goal before the five-minute mark. Drew Doughty, drafted second overall by the Kings in 2008, added a snap shot on what we rate as a 3% chance, one of the less likely goals you'll see. By the second period, even a slap shot from Mikey Anderson, a 1% look in our numbers, found its way in.

The play itself was much closer than the score. The two teams finished almost level in expected goals (the quality of chances taken), LAK at 2.88 and NYR at 2.78. Our simulations, which replay every shot, gave NYR the win 53% of the time. At even strength, NYR held the edge in chances, 2.45 expected goals to 1.53. J.T. Miller fired six shots on goal and scored once, and his best look, a 22% chance, was stopped by Darcy Kuemper. LAK scored on a power play (1 for 3), while NYR scored on its only man advantage. In goal, James Reimer allowed three goals on eight shots, about two more than those shots deserved, and Dylan Garand gave up two on 17.

NYR pulled within 5-3 on Tye Kartye's goal at 16:08 of the third, but Joel Edmundson restored the three-goal margin 29 seconds later. Our facts don't include standings or streaks for either club, so the result stands as one night: a team that scored on nearly everything it got beat a team that created more but couldn't finish.
